title: Synthetic traffic blueprint and deterministic fixture generator for cross-SDK contract validation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: SDK teams maintain separate deterministic fixture sets for unit, integration, and contract tests. Current VCR/mockserver artifacts focus on request/response pairs but lack a first-class representation for streaming frames, partial token emissions, KV cache priming, and in-flight retries/backpressure. This makes it hard to assert cross-language parity for streaming ergonomics, retry semantics, and token-level contract guarantees.

Goal: Define a canonical synthetic-traffic blueprint (an event DSL) and implement a generator tool that emits deterministic fixtures consumable by Python/TS/Go SDK test runners and the CI VCR runner. Fixtures should: canonicalize non-deterministic fields (timestamps, request ids), support partial-frame streaming traces, simulate intermittent 5xxs and connection resets for retry testing, emulate KV cache warm-start snapshots, and include annotations for expected SDK-side behavior (e.g., backpressure, aborted streams, replays).

Success criteria / Acceptance: 
- A documented DSL spec (Confluence) describing event primitives: Request, Response, StreamFrame, NetworkFault, Delay, CachePriming, HeaderVariation.
- A CLI generator (pkg: fixtures-gen) that takes a human-friendly YAML scenario and outputs versioned JSON fixtures that all three SDKs can consume.
- End-to-end contract test in CI that: runs Python/TS/Go example apps against the generated fixture via the mockserver/VCR proxy and asserts: token-level equivalence for completed streams, consistent retry counts, and matching public API errors for aborted streams.
- Improved coverage for streaming ergonomics: chunk boundaries, partial JSON tokens, function call boundaries in streaming mode.

Design trade-offs considered: 
- Option A: Extend existing VCR cassette format. Pros: reuse infra. Cons: cassette format becomes bloated with streaming frame metadata and loses human readability.
- Option B (chosen): New 'synthetic-traffic' JSON schema (derived from DSL) with a compact YAML authoring layer for engineers. Pros: expressive for streaming/faults, easier cross-SDK parsing. Cons: additional converters and migration for old fixtures.

Notes on parity and SDK API surface: the DSL includes an "sdk_hint" field per event that describes expected client behavior (e.g., "should_buffer": true, "retry_on": ["connection_reset","5xx"], "allow_partial_json": true). Each SDK test adapter will translate these hints into SDK assertions and mockserver orchestration. This keeps the generator language-agnostic but testable across runtimes.

Rollout plan: 
1) Spec review with SDK leads and QA (this ticket) 
2) fixtures-gen PoC and YAML -> JSON roundtrip 
3) Python SDK adapter + one contract test PR 
4) TS and Go adapters + CI gating 
5) Migrate 15 highest-value existing VCR tests to new format for validation

Links & artifacts: 
- Confluence (design doc): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Synthetic+Traffic+DSL+Spec 
- PoC generator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fixtures-gen/pull/12 
- Example YAML scenarios: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fixtures-gen/tree/main/examples 
- Mockserver orchestration RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-mockserver-rfc
- Reference issue for streaming timeout alignment: ENG-41207

Safety/Compliance: No customer data in fixtures; canonical datasets only. Fixtures must be scrubbed and contain synthetic ids.
tasks: Draft DSL primitives and publish Confluence spec
Implement CLI generator (yaml -> canonical fixture JSON)
Add parser/adapters for python-sdk test harness
Add parser/adapters for typescript-sdk test harness
Add parser/adapters for go-sdk test harness
Create CI job that runs contract suite against mockserver using generated fixtures
Migrate selected high-value VCR tests to new format
Document best practices and example scenarios for SDK authors
updates: 2025-01-20: Kickoff meeting with SDK leads (Maya, Jorge, Lin) — agreed on new DSL vs extending cassette. Decided to keep YAML authoring for readability.
2025-01-27: PoC generator prototype can emit simple request/response and streaming frames; initial JSON schema v0.1 published on Confluence.

2025-02-03: Maya opened fixtures-gen PR #12 with CLI scaffolding and example scenarios. Feedback from Jorge: include explicit "clock" control for delay events to speed CI. Action: add virtual clock flag to generator.
2025-02-07: Added python adapter prototype and a smoke contract test asserting retry semantics for transient 502 -> success. Found mismatch in TS SDK retry backoff (ENG-50210 created).
qa_plan: QA to run generator against 10 legacy VCR cassettes transformed into the DSL and validate token-level diffs. Create flaky-test checklist and add virtual-clock to speed up delay scenarios in CI.
risks: Migration burden: many existing VCR cassettes must be ported or wrapped
Possible divergence between SDK adapters if sdk_hint semantics are ambiguous
Increased CI runtime if delay/clock control not implemented
mitigation: Start with a small migration batch (15 tests) to validate format
Lock sdk_hint taxonomy in spec and require test adapter lints
Implement virtual-clock feature to collapse delays in CI
